claims.text: Nonstress test (NST): external monitors record fetal HR and contractions and match HR to fetal movements.
claims.quote: A nonstress test records fetal HR and uterine contractions using external electronic monitors and correlates the HR with fetal movements (reported by the mother)
The nonstress test is typically done for 20 minutes (occasionally for 40 minutes).

claims.text: Reactive (reassuring): 2 accelerations of 15 beats/minute over 20 minutes. No accelerations is nonreactive (nonreassuring).
claims.quote: Results are considered reactive (reassuring) if there are 2 accelerations of 15 beats/minute over 20 minutes. Absence of accelerations is considered nonreactive (nonreassuring).

claims.text: Biophysical profile (BPP): usually done after a nonreassuring NST. It adds ultrasound of amniotic fluid volume, fetal movement, tone, and breathing to the NST.
claims.quote: A biophysical profile is usually done after a nonreassuring nonstress test. The biophysical profile adds ultrasonographic assessment of amniotic fluid volume, fetal movement, tone, and breathing to the nonstress test.

claims.text: Used for complicated or high-risk pregnancies, eg, maternal diabetes, hypertension, prior stillbirth, fetal growth restriction, or fetal anomaly.
claims.quote: A nonstress test and biophysical profile are frequently used to monitor complicated or high-risk pregnancies (eg, complicated by maternal diabetes, hypertension, stillbirth in a prior pregnancy, or fetal growth restriction or fetal anomaly).
